items.review_rationale: Read the recursive commutator criterion for order at most k, including its zero-order case requiring S-linearity, and the roles of the original R-linear map D and the S-actions on source and target.

references.context: Module theory: R-linear homomorphism of underlying R-modules obtained by restriction of scalars along R→S
Module theory: S-module homomorphism commuting with scalar action
Algebra: difference of two ways to apply S-action across a homomorphism

references.phrase: order at most k recursively reduces order by one
references.disposition: The recursion holds for every s∈S, not merely a chosen generating subset, and does not assert that D itself is S-linear for k>0.

items.review_rationale: Examined the representing universal property of order-k principal parts with Hom_S(P^k(M),N) naturally identified with all differential operators of order at most k from M to N, for every S-module N.

references.context: Category and module theory: natural isomorphism of functors in target N represented by an S-module

references.disposition: The representation requires compatible bijections for all targets, not merely one chosen N.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed initiality of the local R-algebra R^h among local maps to Henselian local rings, the specified maximal ideal and residue-field condition, and the possible filtered colimit of étale algebras without conflating henselization with completion.

references.context: Category and local algebra: universal initial object among suitable Henselian local R-algebras and local maps

references.phrase: maximal ideal mR^h and residue field R/m
references.context: Commutative algebra: extension of maximal ideal and quotient residue field compatible with the local homomorphism

references.phrase: may be constructed as a filtered colimit
references.disposition: The construction is an alternative presentation using suitable étale neighborhoods, not a claim that any filtered diagram of étale algebras suffices.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed strict henselization relative to a chosen separable closure of the residue field, with universal local lifting compatible with its specified embedding; it is not a construction independent of the chosen geometric residue-field point.

references.phrase: separable closure κ^sep of residue field κ=R/m
references.context: Field theory and local algebra: chosen separable algebraic closure of the residue field of a local ring

references.phrase: local ring homomorphisms compatible with residue embedding
references.context: Local algebra: local morphisms respecting chosen embedding into a separably closed residue field

references.disposition: The residue field is part of the chosen strict henselization data, not merely any algebraic extension of κ.

items.review_rationale: Read the supremum over lengths of strict chains of submodules from zero to M, with infinity when no finite upper bound exists; did not substitute vector-space dimension or ring Krull dimension.

references.phrase: strictly increasing finite chain of submodules
references.context: Order theory and module theory: chain under proper inclusion from zero submodule to whole M

references.phrase: supremum of integers n including unbounded case
references.disposition: Composition length here counts strict inclusions and can be infinite; it is not number of generators.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed both nonzero and absence of nontrivial submodules. A zero module meets the only-submodules condition vacuously but is explicitly excluded from simplicity.

references.phrase: nonzero and only submodules are 0 and M
references.disposition: Nonzero condition is essential, and no assumption that the ring R is a field or the module is finitely generated is made.

items.review_rationale: Read the all-elements quantification in Ann_R(M), distinguishing common annihilators of an entire module from the possibly larger annihilator of an individual element.

references.phrase: scalar product r·m and zero module element
references.context: Module theory: scalar action R×M→M and additive zero

references.disposition: The ideal contains exactly scalars killing every element of M, not just some element.

items.review_rationale: Read the one-element version Ann_R(m) with m fixed, retaining the difference from Ann_R(M) which quantifies over all elements; linked the ambient R-module and ideal notions.

references.context: Module theory: annihilation of one fixed module element by scalars in R

references.disposition: Only scalars annihilating this one m qualify; no quantification over every element of the module is asserted.
